en: The Filipino value of 'Bayanihan' involves the entire community working together, traditionally carrying a whole nipa hut made of bamboo to a new location.
Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence on June 12, 1898, in Kawit, Cavite, ending over 300 years of Spanish colonial rule.
The Philippine Congress is bicameral, consisting of a Senate with 24 elected members and a House of Representatives with over 300 district and party-list representatives.
The Philippines has over 180 distinct native languages, but Filipino and English are the two official languages used in government and education.
The Sinulog Festival in Cebu honors the Santo Niño, drawing over one million attendees annually to its vibrant, nine-day street dancing celebration.
The Ifugao people built the Banaue Rice Terraces over 2,000 years ago, carving approximately 10,000 square kilometers of mountains into stepped agricultural fields.
National hero Jose Rizal wrote his two famous novels, Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo, mastering a total of 22 different languages during his lifetime.
Filipino scientist Dr. Ramon Barba invented the flower induction technique for mangoes in 1974, increasing fruit yields by up to 5 times compared to natural flowering.
National Architect Leandro Locsin designed the Cultural Center of the Philippines complex, which spans 62 hectares and includes 5 main theater buildings.
Under the 1987 Philippine Constitution, citizens must be at least 18 years old and have resided in the country for at least one year to vote.
The Sampaguita, the Philippine national flower, was officially declared the national flower in 1934 and grows as a shrub reaching up to 3 meters tall.
The Treaty of Paris in 1898 transferred the Philippines from Spain to the United States for a payment of exactly 20 million US dollars.
